bench: Five attempts (a01/a03/a04 dry, a02 and a05 engine). a02 with the fixed 0.875 threshold: POSITIVE_CONTROL_FAILED. Only 9 of 390,625 genotypes reach 0.875 on skelA (2.3e-05) and 36 on skelB (9.2e-05), so a 2,000-3,200 evaluation climb expects 0.05 hits; the primary observable was censored in 44 of 48 rows and the identity encoding hit the target in 1 of 4 table x climber cells. Same failure shape as C3-SFE-03 a02 (L3-011): an instrument gated on a fixed constant instead of on the measured state of its own space. a05 (of record) sets the threshold per TABLE by a rule fixed before the run -- the highest battery level at least 0.1% of genotypes reach -- and widens the climbs to 20 restarts x 400 steps and N=50 x G=80. 422 s: tables 349 s (781,250 evaluations), geometry 52 s, climbs 57 s; 48 records, 0 errors. The rule works mechanically and the positive control passes, but it selected a CHANCE-level target on skelB (see below), which is the defect this record reports.
disposition_note: The machine's candidate on the preregistered primary is WEAK_POSITIVE (pooled Spearman rho = -0.568 over 48 rows, declared direction, |rho| >= 0.5). That number is CONFOUNDED and is not usable: it is a two-point correlation between the two score tables, not a correlation over 48 independent rows. skelB has basin share 0.41-0.43 and is trivially easy (median first hit 1-2022); skelA has basin share 0.026-0.034 and is hard (3232-8021). Pooling them produces a strong negative rho by construction. WITHIN table the evidence is one informative cell out of four: skelA first-improvement rho = -0.527 (declared direction, 12 encodings), skelA population rho = +0.187 (wrong sign), skelB first-improvement rho = -0.042, skelB population undefined (every row hits at evaluation 1). INCONCLUSIVE is the honest reading: the out-of-family test was not delivered.
landscape: Two exhaustive 25^4 opcode spaces on the same cell have utterly different geometry, and that difference is the experiment's real content. skelA: basin share 0.026-0.034, deceptive share 0.307-0.331, the 0.125 level (2 of 16 asks correct, above the 1/16 chance floor) reached by 402 genotypes; a first-improvement climber with 8,020 evaluations reaches it in 13 of 36 seeds and a population climber in 30 of 36. skelB: basin share 0.410-0.435, deceptive share 0.000, and its score distribution is BIMODAL -- 8.6% of genotypes sit exactly at the 0.0625 chance level and the next populated level up is reached by 9.2e-05, with nothing measurable in between. The adaptive rule therefore picked chance itself as skelB's target, which every population climb satisfies in its initial sample (median first hit 1). skelB contributes no search information at all. Within skelA the encodings differ only slightly (basin 0.0256 identity to 0.0338 perm_7, accessible variation 1.430-1.451, a 32% relative spread in basin against a 1.5% spread in accessible variation), and the first-improvement climber's median first hit does move with it: the three encodings with the highest basin share include the three fastest cells, the identity and class-grouped encodings are the slowest and hit 0 of 3 seeds. That is the surviving signal, and it is 12 points in one cell.
science: The out-of-family replication of C2-SFE-08's basin-share result is NOT delivered, and the reason is a confound the campaign should have anticipated. The preregistered primary (pooled Spearman rho of basin share against log evaluations-to-threshold over all encoding x table x climber rows) returns -0.568, which clears the declared |rho| >= 0.5 in the declared direction and would replicate campaign 2's -0.59 almost exactly. It is an artefact of pooling two score tables whose difficulty and basin share differ by an order of magnitude: skelB basin 0.41-0.43 and easy, skelA basin 0.026-0.034 and hard. With two strata the pooled statistic has two informative points regardless of how many rows it is computed over. Decomposed within table and climber: skelA first-improvement rho = -0.527 (12 encodings, declared direction, the one cell that replicates), skelA population rho = +0.187, skelB first-improvement rho = -0.042, skelB population undefined. One of four cells replicates; one contradicts in sign; two cannot express the measurement because skelB's target is the chance level. Typed state: READOUT_CANNOT_EXPRESS for skelB. INSTRUMENT DEFECT (a05, now recorded): the adaptive threshold rule takes the highest level at least 0.1% of genotypes reach, but does not require that level to be ABOVE CHANCE. On a bimodal table it therefore selects chance itself and measures time-to-chance. The rule must require threshold > chance (1/16 here) and type the table READOUT_CANNOT_EXPRESS when no such level exists. SECOND INSTRUMENT DEFECT (general): a rank-correlation primary pooled over strata with different difficulty must be declared WITHIN stratum, or the strata must be matched; the campaign-2 result it was testing is itself pooled over one evaluator family and should be re-read with that in mind. Consequence for C3-SFE-07, recorded before that slot runs: its encoding pair is selected from skelA rows only. Must NOT be claimed: that basin share is validated out of family (the pooled number that would say so is confounded); that basin share is refuted (skelA first-improvement replicates at -0.527); that the two climbers disagree about geometry in general (one of them, on the only informative table, is where the signal lives, and n is 12).
